title: Prime coefficients in proper smooth curve families
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $f:C\to S$ a proper smooth morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with nonempty geometrically connected fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] of dimension exactly one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For every prime $\ell$ and every $q\ge0$, the sheaf $R^qf_*\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. No invertibility of $\ell$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0GKV, label lemma-proper-smooth-family-curves; finite-field module form of its constructible abelian conclusion

proof.text: Put $G_q=R^qf_*\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}$ in module sheaves and $A_q=\operatorname{For}(G_q)$. Coefficient forgetting identifies $A_q$ with the abelian higher direct image. At each geometric point $\bar s$, proper base change identifies its stalk with $H^q(C_{\bar s},\mathbf F_\ell)$; inverse image preserves the constant sheaf. The fibre is a smooth proper connected curve over an algebraically closed field, by proper and smooth base-change permanence and the given geometric fibre hypotheses. The curve-finiteness lemma makes these stalks finite for every prime $\ell$, including the residue characteristic.

source.place: Tag 0GKV, label lemma-proper-smooth-family-curves; case (a) finite stalks, also used in case (b)

proof.text: Let $U=D(\ell)\subset S$ and $Z=V(\ell)\hookrightarrow S$ with its closed subscheme structure. Prime proper base change along both inclusions identifies the restrictions of $A_q$ with the higher direct images of the constant sheaf on $C_U$ and $C_Z$; coefficient comparison gives the module identifications for $G_q$. Properness and smooth relative dimension one persist under base change. The geometric fibres are the given fibres after an algebraically closed field extension, so remain nonempty geometrically connected curves. Both bases are Noetherian. A finite constructible module stratification on each piece gives one on $S$ by concatenation: every locally closed constructible subset of either piece is locally closed and constructible in the Noetherian $S$, and its immersion into the piece composes with that piece's inclusion by clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Thus it suffices to treat the two pieces. Empty pieces are permitted. More explicitly, $U$ is locally Noetherian by the open-subscheme clause of [pqf-def-locnoeth], and it is quasi-compact because every open in a Noetherian topological space is quasi-compact. By [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $S$ has Noetherian coordinate ring $A$. On such an affine open, the corresponding closed piece is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/(\ell))$, which is Noetherian: any ascending chain of ideals in the quotient pulls back to an ascending chain of ideals of $A$ and stabilizes. The closed piece is quasi-compact as a closed subset of the Noetherian underlying space. To justify the topological Noetherian assertions, choose a finite affine open cover of $S$. Each affine has Noetherian underlying space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]; an ascending chain of opens stabilizes on each member, hence on their finite union. In such a space every open covering of an open has a finite subcover: the finite unions of its members have a maximal member, which must contain them all. For the quotient-ring check, the ascending-chain condition follows directly from finite generation: the union of a chain is an ideal, and its finite generators lie in one member.

source.place: Tag 0GKV, label lemma-proper-smooth-family-curves; Noetherian reduction to cases (a),(b)

proof.text: On $U$, the input is locally constant and $\ell$ is invertible. The specialization-invariance lemma gives bijective specialization maps in every degree. Coefficient comparison gives the same bijections on module stalks, and Step 1 gives finite stalks. Apply the finite-stalk specialization criterion to the Noetherian $U$ and the finite ring $\mathbf F_\ell$. Hence $G_q|_U$ is finite locally constant. The one-piece stratum proves its constructibility.

On $Z$, put $p=\ell$; $p\cdot1=0$ in its structure sheaf, including if $Z$ is nonreduced. For $q\geq2$, the proper fibre formula and characteristic-$p$ curve vanishing give zero stalks of $A_q|_Z$. Stalk conservativity makes it the zero sheaf. For $q=0$, apply the flat quasi-compact connected-fibre sections lemma to $C_Z\times_ZV\to V$ for every etale object $V\to Z$. The smooth-flat lemma gives flatness, and smooth/proper permanence applies to each of these base changes. Smooth implies flat and proper implies quasi-compact, and these hypotheses persist on base change; its fibres remain the nonempty connected geometric fibres in question. The resulting bijections are the pullback maps on sections of the constant sheaf and commute with restrictions, giving $f_{Z,*}\underline{\mathbf F_p}\cong\underline{\mathbf F_p}$. Coefficient forgetting reflects the isomorphisms. Degree zero and degrees at least two are therefore constructible with one stratum.

source.place: Tag 0GKV, label lemma-proper-smooth-family-curves; case (b), degrees zero and at least two

proof.text:
For degree one on $Z$, the scheme Artin--Schreier section-data and exactness lemmas on $C_Z$ give $0\to\underline{\mathbf F_p}\to\mathcal O_{C_Z,\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{F-1}\mathcal O_{C_Z,\mathrm{et}}\to0$, where $F=\wp+1$ is sectionwise $p$-th power. Use the same lifted associated structure sheaf as in the section-data lemma and the structure-direct-image input, so no coefficient-universe change occurs. Abelian direct image is additive left exact, and abelian sheaves have enough injectives. Its right derived delta-functor gives an exact segment, hence the short exact sequence
$$0\to\operatorname{Coker}(F-1:f_{Z,*}\mathcal O_{C_Z,\mathrm{et}}\to f_{Z,*}\mathcal O_{C_Z,\mathrm{et}})\to A_1|_Z\to\operatorname{Ker}(F-1:R^1f_{Z,*}\mathcal O_{C_Z,\mathrm{et}}\to R^1f_{Z,*}\mathcal O_{C_Z,\mathrm{et}})\to0.$$
Exactness at the two adjacent terms identifies the image of the connecting map with that cokernel, and the image of its successor with that kernel. This is in abelian sheaves; it does not assert finite prime-field dimension of the structure sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0GKV, label lemma-proper-smooth-family-curves; case (b), Artin--Schreier exact segment

proof.text: The structure-direct-image lemma identifies the first repeated term with $\mathcal O_{Z,\mathrm{et}}$ and the second with $E_{\mathrm{et}}$ for a finite locally free module $E$. On the first term $F$ is $p$-th power. Use the higher-direct-image presheaf lemma to express the second term as the sheafification of $V\mapsto H^1(C_Z\times_ZV,\mathcal O_{C_Z,\mathrm{et}})$. On the second term $F$ is Frobenius-semilinear: on every etale base object and for every base section $a$, the sectionwise identity $F\circ m_{f^*a}=m_{f^*(a^p)}\circ F$ induces the same identity on cohomology by functoriality. The natural scalar action specified in the structure-direct-image lemma is the action of these multiplication maps. Thus $F(ae)=a^pF(e)$. For a morphism $W\to V$ of etale base objects, pullback sends $a$ to $a|_W$, sends $a^p$ to $(a|_W)^p$, and sends the sectionwise $p$-th-power map to the same map over $W$. The cohomology restriction maps therefore respect the displayed identity. A section of the associated sheaf is locally represented by a presheaf section, so the identity holds locally for every section and hence holds in the sheaf. Apply the Frobenius vector-bundle lemma to $\mathcal O_Z$ and to $E$. The first application makes the cokernel zero; the second makes the kernel constructible as an abelian sheaf. The exact segment then identifies $A_1|_Z$ with that kernel.

source.place: Tag 0GKV, label lemma-proper-smooth-family-curves; case (b), structure cohomology and final application of 0GKU

proof.text: On each finite abelian constant stratum of $A_1|_Z$, choose its additive constant charts with values $B$. Each element of $B$ is killed by $p$: on a nonempty chart read $pG_1=0$ at a geometric stalk, identified with $B$ by the constant-stalk lemma. Empty charts may be omitted. Give $B$ the forced $\mathbf F_p$-action $(a\bmod p)b=ab$, with the right side repeated addition. Every additive chart map commutes with this action, since every element of $\mathbf F_p$ is an integer multiple of $1$. Thus the same charts are finite constant module charts. Coefficient forgetting commutes with the inverse images on strata, so $G_1|_Z$ is constructible in the module sense. Step 4 treats the other degrees on $Z$, and Step 3 treats every degree on $U$. Concatenate their finite stratifications as in Step 2. This proves every $q\geq0$ on $S$ without requiring invertibility of $\ell$; zero sheaves and empty pieces cause no exception.
